panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panoramic low-power view of the renal biopsy tissue cylinder from a patient with familial LCAT deficiency. The in-text refers to Figure 2 as a whole, confirming mesangial expansion and foamy lipid deposits in the biopsy. Specific findings are better appreciated at higher magnification in panels B-D. B: Histology of renal biopsy showing glomerular involvement with expansion of the mesangium, a classic finding in familial LCAT deficiency with renal disease. C: High-power histology of renal biopsy showing foamy lipid deposits at capillary and mesangial level, consistent with glomerular foam cells in familial LCAT deficiency. D: High-power histology of renal biopsy showing foamy lipid deposits at capillary and mesangial level, consistent with glomerular foam cells in familial LCAT deficiency.

in_text_mentions: Given the patient’s history of corneal opacity since childhood (Figure 2), lipid abnormalities with a marked reduction in HDL-C, and nephrotic syndrome, hereditary lipoprotein metabolic disorders, particularly LCAT deficiency-related nephropathy, were strongly suspected. To clarify the pathological nature of the renal involvement, a renal biopsy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed glomerular lipid deposition, confirming the diagnosis of LCAT deficiency-related renal damage (Figures 3–5).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: H&E renal biopsy from a patient diagnosed with familial LCAT deficiency; foamy endothelial cells correspond to glomerular foam cells, a classic histologic feature of LCAT deficiency nephropathy. B: PAS-stained renal biopsy showing mesangial proliferation, consistent with mesangial expansion in LCAT deficiency-related nephropathy. C: PASM-stained renal biopsy from the LCAT deficiency patient showing basement membrane vacuolization and double-track sign, a recognized histologic feature of LCAT deficiency nephropathy; not directly covered by the vocabulary. D: Masson's stain of the patient's renal biopsy showing no immune deposits, a supportive negative feature in the diagnostic workup of LCAT deficiency nephropathy; real patient histology with no fitting exclusion reason. E: Oil red O stain of the patient's renal biopsy demonstrating glomerular lipid droplets, confirming glomerular lipidosis/foam cells in LCAT deficiency. F: Oil...

panels.figure_caption: Light microscopy findings on renal biopsy. (A) H&E staining: dilated capillary loops with vacuolar thrombus-like material (black arrows) and foamy endothelial cells (white arrows). (B) PAS staining: mesangial proliferation (black arrows) and basement membrane thickening (white arrows). (C) PASM staining: vacuolar areas in basement membrane (white arrows) with double-track sign (black arrows). (D) Masson’s stain: negative for immune deposits. (E,F) Oil red O stain: positive lipid droplets in glomeruli and tubular cells (black arrows). ×400.
